findings.title: Tests rewrite the live application Orchestrator/DecisionStore/registries and leave the singleton Orchestrator with a dead tick
findings.description: Three test modules take the application-supervised singleton `Aiur.Orchestrator` (and `Aiur.DecisionStore`) with `Process.whereis/1` and rewrite 12-16 internal State fields with `:sys.replace_state`. Their setup cancels the singleton's pending tick timer, and on_exit restores the *original* state snapshot, which still carries the cancelled `tick_timer_ref` and old `tick_token`. After restore no `{:tick, token}` is in flight; `Lifecycle.wake_tick/1` only moves an already-scheduled tick (returns state unchanged when `next_poll_due_at_ms <= target`), so the singleton stops polling until something calls `request_refresh`. This is a latch in the shared suite state, order-dependent for every later module that relies on the app Orchestrator. Other shared singletons are mutated the same way: dispatcher_test creates blocking Decisions on the global DecisionStore via `ToolExecutor` emit_event and never answers them (4 per run, lines 2810-2817 and 3049-3055); slot_policy_test `setup` kills every process in the app-global SlotRegistry and two tests `:sys.suspend` the registry partitions; token_registry_test writes/deletes (`delete_stale(1, 2)`) in the live TokenRegistry with inline (not on_exit) cleanup; session_writer_registry_test calls `delete_all()` on the live registry.
findings.evidence: self_pause_answer_test.exs:11-12 `orchestrator = Process.whereis(Orchestrator); original = :sys.get_state(orchestrator)`; :29 `if is_reference(state.tick_timer_ref), do: Process.cancel_timer(state.tick_timer_ref)`; :48 `:sys.replace_state(orchestrator, fn _ -> original end)`. resume_control_regression_test.exs:21-22,32 same shape; :57 `:sys.replace_state(pid, fn _state -> %{original_state | snapshot_generation: snapshot_generation} end)`. lifecycle.ex:346-357 `def wake_tick(%State{tick_timer_ref: timer_ref, poll_frozen: frozen} = state) when is_reference(timer_ref) and frozen != true ... if is_integer(state.next_poll_due_at_ms) and state.next_poll_due_at_ms <= target_ms, do: state`. :sys.replace_state counts: self_pause_answer_test 30 :sys calls, resume_control_regression_test 21, orphaned_workers_test 12. Contrast: correlated_replay_wake_test.exs:94-111 starts its own `Orchestrator.start_link(name: name)` and only rewrites that private instance.
findings.recommendation: Never rewrite application singletons from tests. Give each such case its own named Orchestrator/DecisionStore (the pattern correlated_replay_wake_test.exs:94 and global_pause_test already use: `Orchestrator.start_link(name: name, initial_poll?: false)`, `DecisionStore` with `name: nil, state_dir: ...`). If a singleton must be touched, restore by calling `Lifecycle.schedule_tick/2` (or `request_refresh`) in on_exit instead of reinstating a stale timer ref. Answer or delete every Decision a test files; inject a registry name into SlotPolicy/TokenRegistry/SessionWriterRegistry so tests use a private registry.
findings.refactor_hint: Blocks carving orchestrator/opencode into packages: these tests depend on the whole Aiur application tree being booted and on the exact State field layout. Make Orchestrator, DecisionStore and the opencode registries startable with a name/registry option and have the package test helpers start private instances.

findings.title: Production code reads 41 test-seam keys from the shared :aiur application env; tests in this unit set 40 distinct keys 197 times
findings.description: Dependency injection for tests is done through VM-global `Application.put_env(:aiur, ...)`, read by production at call time. Any test touching one of these keys must be `async: false`, must save/restore by hand, and still leaks into application processes that run concurrently. Across this unit tests set 40 distinct keys in 197 put_env calls in 27 files (top: loadavg_source_override 17, build_order_planning_pack 17, file_descriptor_sample_override 15, memory_tracker_issues 14, global_pause_store_path 10). In src/lib, 41 distinct keys ending in `_override`, `_fun`, `_module`, `_recorder`, `_verifier` or `test_options` are read with Application.get_env. `:github_client_module` is resolved independently in two modules (github/tracker.ex:195 and orchestrator/human_review.ex:176). PlanningSource needs 5 keys plus `AIUR_BUILD_ORDER_DIRS` and `:repo_base_root` to be steered, so planning_source_test juggles 7 globals per test.
findings.evidence: `grep -oh 'Application.put_env(:aiur, :[a-z_?]+'` over the unit: 40 distinct keys, 197 sites. system_load.ex:34 `Application.get_env(:aiur, :loadavg_source_override, fn -> File.read("/proc/loadavg") end)`; memory/tracker.ex:166 `Application.get_env(:aiur, :memory_tracker_issues, [])`; agent_control_cli.ex:3186 `Application.get_env(:aiur, :agent_control_cli_resume_fun, &AgentChat.resume_with_receipt/1).(identifier)`. `grep -rhoE 'Application\.(get|fetch)_env\(:aiur, :[a-z_?]+(override|_fun|_module|_recorder|_verifier|test_options)' src/lib | sort -u | wc -l` = 41.
findings.recommendation: Replace env-var seams with explicit injection: pass probes/clients/recorders through function opts or a per-process config struct built once at GenServer init (the Dispatcher already accepts `admission_probes_fun:`, `runner:`, `issue_fetcher:` opts; finish that and delete the env fallbacks). Group the remaining knobs per future package (e.g. `Aiur.Host.Probes` for loadavg/proc_stat/meminfo/fd/build_gate) so each package owns one config struct. Keep a single resolver for the GitHub client module.
findings.refactor_hint: Shared mutable `:aiur` env is exactly the cross-package global the carve must remove: each package needs its own app env or explicit config. Inventory the 41 seam keys and assign each to its owning package before moving code.

findings.title: Aiur.TestSupport is a 1,663-line god helper that 37 files in this unit `use`, including 4 that need none of it
findings.description: `use Aiur.TestSupport` expands to a sync `use ExUnit.Case`, aliases 20 modules (Linear.Client, Codex.CodingAgent, StatusDashboard, HttpServer...), writes a workflow file, force-reloads WorkflowStore (15 s timeout), resets GitHub ResourceStore/AuthPreflight/PollCadence/DispatchAuthorization, restarts app children if down and stops the HTTP server, for every test. In this unit 31 orchestrator files, 5 opencode files and 1 aiur_web file use it. protocol_test (pure Protocol builders), token_registry_test, ticket_context_presenter_test (pure presenter, no Config/Application reads) and bridge_test reference no workflow/config/app state at all, yet pay the setup and are forced sync. `__using__(_opts)` drops its options, so 5 files that write `use Aiur.TestSupport, async: false` (bridge, config, protocol, token_registry, github_budget_pause) pass a no-op, and `async: true` would be silently ignored the same way; 3 files carry comments explaining that the module is not async.
findings.evidence: test_support.exs:228 `defmacro __using__(_opts) do` / :230 `use ExUnit.Case`; :251-259 imports; :261-380 setup (workflow root, capture_app_env, reset_global_state!, write_workflow_file!, ensure_runtime_children_running, force_reload, stop_default_http_server). Per-directory counts in this unit: orchestrator 31/69 files use it, opencode 5/36, aiur_web 1/9. `grep -cE 'write_workflow_file|Workflow\.|Config\.|WorkflowStore|Orchestrator|start_supervised|AlertLedger|Exchange|Alerts\.'` = 0 for bridge_test, protocol_test, token_registry_test, ticket_context_presenter_test.
findings.recommendation: Split TestSupport into small opt-in helpers: `Aiur.Test.WorkflowCase` (workflow file + WorkflowStore), `Aiur.Test.GlobalStateReset` (the persistent_term resets), `Aiur.Test.Tmp` (tmp_root!), `Aiur.Test.AppChildren` (ensure_*_running). Make `__using__` honour `async:` or raise when given it. Move pure-function tests (protocol, presenter, token registry with a private registry) to `use ExUnit.Case, async: true`.
findings.refactor_hint: Each future package needs its own test support; today an opencode or aiur_web test cannot compile without the orchestrator, GitHub and WorkflowStore modules TestSupport aliases. Carve the helper along the same package lines before moving the tests.

findings.title: assert_receive with the 100 ms default waits on messages sent by other processes (≈70 verified sites); 257 bare assert_receive in 39 files overall
findings.description: Parsed count across the unit: 366 assert_receive (257 without a timeout, in 39 files) and 112 refute_receive (61 without a timeout, 17 files). Most bare sites follow a synchronous call and are harmless, but several families wait on a different process with only 100 ms: the dispatcher's runner runs inside `Task.Supervisor.start_child(Aiur.TaskSupervisor, ...)`, so every `assert_receive {:agent_runner_run, ...}` races the task start (9 bare sites in dispatcher_test, 2 in dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test, 1 in dispatcher_stale_blocked_by_test); dispatcher_test:648 waits 1_000 ms for the same message, so the file is inconsistent with itself. `start_initial_ci_readiness_check` and `maybe_warn_ci_readiness` spawn the readiness scan (dispatcher_test 867-868, 981). realtime_test has 44 bare waits on the session process (its moduledoc says the suite runs 'without a clock', but each is a 100 ms clock); tts_test has 9 on the spawned TTS process; retry_engine_test 1163/1187 wait on the Ownership guardian.
findings.evidence: dispatcher.ex:2503 `case Task.Supervisor.start_child(Aiur.TaskSupervisor, fn -> runner.(issue, recipient, ...)`. dispatcher_test.exs:426 `assert_receive {:agent_runner_run, dispatched, _recipient, _opts}` vs :648 `assert_receive {:agent_runner_run, ^ticket_id}, 1_000`. realtime_test.exs moduledoc: 'exercised without a socket and without a clock'; 44 bare assert_receive. Worst files by bare count: realtime_test 44, comment_wake_test 24+15 refute, merged_ticket_reconciler_test 24+15, dispatcher_test 21+1, startup_claim_reconciler_test 14+2, issue_sync_test 14.
findings.recommendation: For cross-process messages use the existing `receive_barrier/1` from TestSupport (no wall clock) or an explicit monitor/`:DOWN`; for messages produced synchronously use `assert_received`. Do not fix this by raising ExUnit's global assert_receive_timeout. Add a Credo check or grep gate: bare `assert_receive` after a call that spawns (Task.Supervisor, Realtime.start, TTS.start) must use receive_barrier.
findings.refactor_hint: Move `receive_barrier/1` out of the god TestSupport into a tiny shared `Aiur.Test.Receive` module that every package's tests can import.

findings.title: Process.sleep used for synchronization and to age records past wall-clock TTLs (42 sites in 16 files)
findings.description: dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test sets `:blocked_by_max_age_ms` to 100 and sleeps 150 ms three times to make a real ResourceStore record stale, and sleeps 2 ms three times so two monotonic-millisecond timestamps differ; both depend on scheduler timing and silently change meaning if production reads a different clock. slot_test (4 sites) and session_writer_test (1) build a 'dead pid' with `spawn(fn -> :ok end); Process.sleep(10)`, which is not guaranteed under load (slot_test:68-70 does not even check liveness). slot_policy_test:327 proves 'nothing started' by sleeping 100 ms. server_test polls a real sqlite db and OS processes at 100 ms × 40.
findings.evidence: dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test.exs:116 `Application.put_env(:aiur, :blocked_by_max_age_ms, 100)` ... :125 `Process.sleep(150)`; :212,:237,:248 `Process.sleep(2)`. slot_test.exs:50-52 `fake = spawn(fn -> :ok end); Process.sleep(10); refute Process.alive?(fake)`. Correct pattern already in the unit: slot_policy_test.exs:476-481 `dead_pid/0` monitors and waits for `:DOWN`.
findings.recommendation: Inject a clock (`now_ms_fun`) into ResourceStore/BoundedBlockedBy freshness checks instead of sleeping past a TTL; for strict ordering pass explicit timestamps. Replace sleep-based dead pids with one shared `dead_pid/0` (monitor + `:DOWN`). Replace negative sleeps with a synchronous probe (`:sys.get_state/1` after the broadcast is processed).
findings.refactor_hint: Freshness/TTL logic in the GitHub cache layer should take a clock seam when it moves into its own package; a shared `Aiur.Test.Process` helper (dead_pid, await_down) belongs in the common test support.

findings.title: refute_receive on a 60-second self-timer can never fail; the tests do not check the timer was cancelled
findings.description: Two tests schedule `Process.send_after(self(), msg, 60_000)`, hand the ref to production code that should cancel it, then `refute_receive msg` with the 100 ms default. The message would not arrive for 60 s whether or not production cancels the timer, so the refutation passes with the cancellation reverted. The same unit already has the falsifiable pattern (`Process.read_timer(timer_ref) == false`) in comment_wake_test.
findings.evidence: lifecycle_test.exs:17 `old_timer = Process.send_after(self(), :superseded_tick, 60_000)` ... :27 `refute_receive :superseded_tick`. retry_engine_test.exs:1207 `timer_ref = Process.send_after(self(), :unexpected_retry, 60_000)` ... :1262 `refute_receive :unexpected_retry`. comment_wake_test.exs:763 `assert Process.read_timer(timer_ref) == false`.
findings.recommendation: Assert `Process.read_timer(ref) == false` (cancelled) instead of refuting the message, and mutation-check both tests by deleting the production `Process.cancel_timer` call.
findings.refactor_hint: Local test fix; no package impact.

findings.title: Placeholder tests assert only that a function exists or returns a type, and one moduledoc claims coverage that is not there
findings.description: session_gc_test's moduledoc says it is 'Regression coverage for T1 + T2' (GC deletes only Aiur-owned sessions not in the active set) but its only test is `function_exported?(SessionGC, :run, 1)`. workspace_cleanup_test is the same existence check. slot_test's 'PubSub event topology' test broadcasts the four events itself and asserts it receives them, so it tests Phoenix.PubSub, not Slot; the slots_topic test asserts only `is_binary`. hidden_window/session_writer_registry assert `is_binary`/`is_list`. no_leaks_test's first test iterates `for {key, %{"name" => name}} <- models` and passes vacuously if the models map is empty or names are missing; its contract is also covered in protocol_test.exs:37.
findings.evidence: session_gc_test.exs:26 `assert function_exported?(SessionGC, :run, 1)`; workspace_cleanup_test.exs:7 `assert function_exported?(WorkspaceCleanup, :cleanup_terminal_issue_artifacts, 2)`; slot_test.exs:120-129 `Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(Aiur.PubSub, topic, {:slot_attach_added, 1, "issue-1"})` ... `assert_receive {:slot_attach_added, 1, "issue-1"}, 500`.
findings.recommendation: Delete existence-only tests or replace them with behaviour tests (SessionGC's filter via an injected session lister; WorkspaceCleanup against a tmp workspace; Slot events by driving the slot helper that broadcasts). Make no_leaks assert `map_size(models) > 0` and fold it into protocol_test.
findings.refactor_hint: These inflate apparent coverage of opencode modules that will move into an opencode package; the carve should not count them as protection.

findings.title: Exchange subscribe/unsubscribe teardown copied 69 times in this unit (109 across the tree) and Publisher.set_tracked_fn reset 138 times although TestSupport already resets it
findings.description: Every event-asserting test repeats: `Publisher.set_tracked_fn(fn _ -> true end)`, one or more `:ok = Exchange.subscribe(topic)`, and an on_exit that resets the tracked fn again and loops `for pattern <- Exchange.bindings_for(self()), do: Exchange.unsubscribe(pattern)`. Teardown loop counts in this unit: issue_sync_test 38, dispatcher_test 11, reconciler_test 8, retry_engine_test 7, operator_messages/alerts_test 3, pr_anchored_test 1, github_budget_pause_test 1 (69; 109 in 27 files tree-wide). set_tracked_fn calls: issue_sync_test 76, dispatcher_test 22, reconciler_test 16, retry_engine_test 14, alerts_test 6, pr_anchored 2, github_budget_pause 2. All of these modules use TestSupport, whose `reset_global_state!/0` already calls `EventsPublisher.set_tracked_fn(fn _ -> true end)` in setup and on_exit.
findings.evidence: issue_sync_test.exs:18-31 (full block); test_support.exs:209 `EventsPublisher.set_tracked_fn(fn _ -> true end)` inside reset_global_state!/0 and :355 in on_exit. `grep -c 'Exchange.bindings_for(self())'` per file as listed.
findings.recommendation: Add `subscribe_events!(topics)` to the shared test support that subscribes and registers the unsubscribe on_exit, and delete the redundant set_tracked_fn calls. One helper replaces ~200 lines in this unit.
findings.refactor_hint: Put the helper next to Aiur.Events in the future events package's test support so orchestrator and web packages import it rather than copying.

findings.title: Hand-rolled Application-env save/restore in 55 sites across 18 files, plus re-isolation of keys TestSupport already isolates
findings.description: `previous = Application.get_env(:aiur, k)` + on_exit restore appears 55 times in 18 files (dispatcher_test 11, global_pause_test 8, lifetime_dispatch_budget_test 7, planning_source_test 4, dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test 4, control_lifecycle_store_test 4 ...). The two-clause restore helper is redefined under three names: `restore_app_env/2` (dispatcher_test, dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test, dispatcher_stale_blocked_by_test, opencode/config_test, bridge_port_test), `restore_application_env/2` (global_pause_test, retry_engine_test), `restore_env/2` (control_lifecycle_store_test) and single-key variants (stream_policy_test, server_test). Several save keys that TestSupport already captures and restores per test: dispatcher_test saves/restores `:loadavg_source_override`/`:proc_stat_source_override` and re-sets the quiet loadavg 14 times; global_pause_test saves `:global_pause_store_path` 3 times; `restore_workflow_file_after_test/0` (5 calls) and the `original_workflow` restores in both blocked_by tests rewrite a per-test workflow file that TestSupport deletes on exit.
findings.evidence: dispatcher_test.exs:65-71 seven `previous_* = Application.get_env`; :2935-2936 `defp restore_app_env(key, nil), do: Application.delete_env(:aiur, key)`. test_support.exs:86-101 `@isolated_app_env_keys [... :build_gate_dir_override, :global_pause_store_path, ... :loadavg_source_override, :proc_stat_source_override ...]`. `grep -c 'loadavg_source_override, fn -> {:ok, "0.0 0.0 0.0 1/1 1'` dispatcher_test = 14 (TestSupport installs the same quiet source).
findings.recommendation: Add `put_app_env!(key, value)` (save + on_exit restore, like the existing `put_runtime_state_dir!/1`) and `put_system_env!(name, value)`; delete the local restore helpers and the redundant re-isolation of keys listed in `@isolated_app_env_keys`.
findings.refactor_hint: Goes away naturally if tests-3-02 (env seams -> injected config) is done; until then a single helper keeps the number of places to update small during the move.

findings.title: Six private polling helpers with different semantics (flunk vs false, attempts vs deadline, 5-100 ms steps)
findings.description: `wait_until/2` (2 copies: one flunks, one asserts), `eventually/2` (6 copies in this unit, 22 tree-wide: attempt-count with 10/20/100 ms sleeps, or deadline-based), `wait_until_timer_fired/2`, plus bespoke `await_*` loops (server_test, slot_policy_test, orphaned_workers_test). The copies disagree on failure mode: dispatcher_test flunks with 'condition was not reached', retry_engine_test/server_test return false and rely on the caller's `assert`, reconcile_test asserts the last value. Total budget varies from 0.5 s to 4 s for similar conditions.
findings.evidence: dispatcher_test.exs:51-61 `defp wait_until(fun, attempts \\ 200) ... Process.sleep(10)`; server_test.exs:432-443 `defp eventually(fun, attempts \\ 40) ... Process.sleep(100)`; slot_policy_test.exs:460 `defp eventually(fun, timeout \\ 2_000)` deadline-based. Tree-wide: `grep -rl 'defp eventually' src/test | wc -l` = 22; `defp wait_until` = 12.
findings.recommendation: Provide one `Aiur.Test.Eventually.assert_eventually(fun, timeout: ms, message: ...)` (deadline-based, flunks with the last observed value) and delete the local copies. Prefer event-driven waits (monitors, telemetry, receive_barrier) where the production code can emit a signal.
findings.refactor_hint: Common test-support primitive for every package; ship it before splitting test suites so each package does not grow its own copy.

findings.title: The 13-key admission-probes fixture is copied 10 times in dispatcher_test and has drifted (3 copies lack github_quota)
findings.description: The map returned by `admission_probes_fun` (memory_mb, memory_threshold_mb, fd_sample, runnable, run_queue_threshold, schedulers, load, load_threshold, build_status, provider_backends, github_quota, cpu_snapshot, target) is written out literally 10 times in dispatcher_test, twice more in dispatch_policy_test with a different key set (cpu_headroom, queued_demand?), and once each in pr_anchored_test and agent_control_cli_test. The copies at dispatcher_test 1630, 2238 and 2305 omit `github_quota`, so those cases exercise a probe shape production never produces and cannot reach the GitHub-quota gate. A new probe key must be added to every copy by hand.
findings.evidence: Scan of dispatcher_test for `memory_threshold_mb:` blocks: 1529 has github_quota, 1635 no, 1837 yes, 1993 yes, 2069 yes, 2154 yes, 2241 no, 2308 no, 2348 yes, 3000 yes. `grep -rn 'memory_threshold_mb:' src/test` also hits pr_anchored_test and agent_control_cli_test.
findings.recommendation: Add `probes(overrides \\ %{})` built from one canonical default (ideally a `DispatchPolicy.Probes` struct in production with `@enforce_keys`, so a missing key fails to compile) and have every test override only the keys it varies. Reuse `contended_probes/2` (dispatcher_test:2996) as the starting point.
findings.refactor_hint: The probe map is the contract between host-sampling code and dispatch policy; making it a struct gives the future dispatch/admission package a typed boundary.

findings.title: Domain fixture builders (tracker_identity, issue, running_entry, base_state, at/1) redefined per file with divergent defaults
findings.description: `tracker_identity/1` is redefined in 6 files of this unit (19 tree-wide) with different owner/repository/provider_id conventions ("owner"/"repository"/"I-<id>", "owner"/"repo"/"I_kwDO<id>", "its-everdred"/"aiur"/"node-<id>"; reconciler_test hardcodes identifier "42" for every identity). `issue/1,2` exists in 7 files (17 tree-wide), `running_entry` in 9 (22 tree-wide) with different control maps, and comment_wake_test/comment_polling_test each spell out a 27-field `%State{}` base. `defp at(seconds)` anchored on fixed dates is copied in tracker_health_test, delivery_mode_test, interval_policy_test and mode_registry_test.
findings.evidence: Helper definition counts from `grep -l 'defp tracker_identity'` (6 in unit), `'defp issue('` (7), `'defp running_entry'` (9). comment_wake_test.exs:9-40 base_state sets todo_over_capacity_alert_active, agent_totals, codex_rate_limits ... github_command_scan_since explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Create `Aiur.Test.Fixtures` (tracker_identity/1, issue/2 with keyword overrides, running_entry/2 with a working/paused control default, orchestrator_state/1) and migrate files incrementally; drop explicit default-valued State fields in favour of `%State{}` + overrides.
findings.refactor_hint: Fixtures for Issue/TrackerIdentity belong with the tracker/core package; orchestrator-state fixtures with the orchestrator package.

findings.title: issue_sync_test calls the 7-arity sync_polled_issue_state 40 times with the same five no-op lambdas, mirroring a positional arity ladder in production
findings.description: IssueSync exposes `sync_polled_issue_state` at arities 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7, each `@doc false` clause filling the next positional function with a default (DispatchPolicy.terminal_state_set, CurrentRunMembership.mark_reconciled/1, set_terminal_verification_pending/2). Tests therefore pass 7 positional arguments; 40 calls in issue_sync_test repeat `fn _ -> {:ok, []} end, fn _identity, _lifecycle -> :ok end, MapSet.new(["done"]), fn _ -> :ok end, fn _identity, _pending? -> :ok end`. The dependency-paused running entry map is also written out 13 times in the same file.
findings.evidence: `grep -c 'IssueSync.sync_polled_issue_state(' issue_sync_test.exs` = 40; `grep -c 'blocker_pause_generation: 1,'` = 13. issue_sync.ex:627 `def sync_polled_issue_state(%State{} = state, issues, fetch_issue_states_fun, observe_membership_fun)`, :646 (5-arity), :675 (6-arity), :706 (7-arity).
findings.recommendation: Collapse the ladder into `sync_polled_issue_state(state, issues, opts \\ [])` with keyword seams and defaults, and add a test helper `sync(state, issues, overrides)`; add `paused_on_blocker(agent, issue, blocker)` for the repeated entry.
findings.refactor_hint: Keyword-opts seams are easier to keep stable across a package boundary than positional arity ladders; do it before moving IssueSync.

findings.title: Six test files exceed 1,000 lines and test several modules each (dispatcher_test 3,197 lines / 93 tests / 16 describes)
findings.description: dispatcher_test (3,197 lines, 93 tests) covers decline alerts, blocked_by gate, blocking-Command gate (505-835), CI readiness (844-1010), candidate fetch, prewarm halt (1174-1403), CPU/memory/FD admission and capacity holds (1405-2566, ~1,160 lines), thrash budget, attempt provenance (2627-2884) and revalidation, and calls IssueSync 16 times and Orchestrator.handle_info once. issue_sync_test (3,032 lines, 88 tests) mixes dependency pause/resume, a PushRouting describe (460-636) although push_routing_test.exs exists, capacity/fleet starvation alerts (~830 lines), observed-error attentions, idle terminal verification, contradictory-label healing (2362-2799) and stranded reconciliation (2801-2952). retry_engine_test (1,774 lines, 22 describes) also drives RateLimitFallback.reconcile, Dispatcher.do_dispatch_issue and SessionLifecycle. comment_wake_test 1,553 lines / 65 tests; reconciler_test 1,057 / 35; dispatch_policy_test 1,041 / 62.
findings.evidence: Line/test counts from wc -l and `grep -cE '^\s*test "'`: dispatcher 3197/93, issue_sync 3032/88, retry_engine 1774/59, comment_wake 1553/65, reconciler 1057/35, dispatch_policy 1041/62. Module reference counts in dispatcher_test: Dispatcher 124, IssueSync 16, SessionLifecycle 4, DispatchPolicy 4.
findings.recommendation: Split by responsibility and by module under test: dispatcher/{admission,ci_readiness,decision_gate,prewarm,provenance}_test.exs; issue_sync/{dependency_resume,capacity_starvation,label_healing,stranded,terminal_verification}_test.exs; move the PushRouting describe to push_routing_test.exs and the capacity-starvation cases from dispatcher_test to issue_sync; move fallback-replacement cases from retry_engine_test to rate_limit_fallback_test.
findings.refactor_hint: Split along the same seams as the production modules (Dispatcher 2,670 lines, IssueSync 2,295 lines) so each extracted production module takes its tests with it.

findings.title: Tests reach internals: @doc false public seams, direct GenServer callback calls, :sys.get_state field reads
findings.description: Dispatcher has 26 `@doc false` public functions; for 10 of them (check_initial_ci_readiness, dispatch_candidate_poll, dispatch_or_hold, emit_prewarm_blocked_alert, fetch_candidate_issues, maybe_warn_ci_readiness, monitor_without_candidates, reconcile_merged_tickets, start_initial_ci_readiness_check, dispatch_with_dependency_gate) no other lib module calls `Dispatcher.<fn>` — they are public only so tests can reach them. session_writer_test calls `SessionWriter.handle_info/2` 18 times with a hand-built state (`build_state/1`), so any State field rename breaks the test without a behaviour change. server_test reads `:sys.get_state(server).port_ref`; orphaned_workers_test reads `:sys.get_state(orchestrator).running` and `.poll_cycles_completed`.
findings.evidence: Scan of dispatcher.ex: 26 functions follow `@doc false`; external `Dispatcher.<fn>` callers in src/lib = 0 for the 10 listed. `grep -c 'handle_info(' session_writer_test.exs` = 18.
findings.recommendation: Test through the module's public API or extract the internally-tested units into their own modules with a real public API (e.g. `Dispatcher.CiReadiness`, `Dispatcher.PrewarmGate`, `Dispatcher.Admission`), then make the remaining helpers `defp`. For GenServers, test via `send/2` + a synchronous call rather than calling callbacks with a fabricated state.
findings.refactor_hint: The @doc false surface is effectively a second, undocumented API that the carve must preserve or break; extracting the tested units first makes the orchestrator package boundary explicit.

findings.title: async comment_wake_test depends on the global tracker config and the global Logger, and asserts through log text
findings.description: The module is `async: true`, yet several tests only pass because the ambient tracker 'fails the write' (comments: 'The unset tracker fails the write (permanently, here a 404)') and they assert `log =~ "rework transition skipped"` as proof the write was attempted. The file itself notes it 'cannot be swapped for a recording fake without serialising the file' because `Tracker.update_issue_state/2` is hard-wired at comment_wake.ex:1425 while the other seams ride inside the event map (`:issue_state_fetcher`, `:open_pr_fetcher`, `:unresolved_threads_fetcher`, `:emit_alert_fun`). `capture_log/1` captures the VM-global Logger (planning_source_test.exs:846-848 documents this, #1747), so in an async module 27 `assert log =~` and 14 `refute log =~` on generic strings can be satisfied or broken by a concurrent test.
findings.evidence: comment_wake_test.exs:2 `use ExUnit.Case, async: true`; :373-376 comment 'The unset tracker fails the write (permanently, here a 404)'; :395 `assert log =~ "rework transition skipped"`; :464-466 'the tracker adapter is global config and this module is `async: true`, so it cannot be swapped for a recording fake'. comment_wake.ex:1425 `case Tracker.update_issue_state(to_string(issue_key), "rework") do`. Counts: 24 capture_log/with_log, 27 assert-log, 14 refute-log.
findings.recommendation: Add an `:update_issue_state_fun` seam to the rework path (the merged-PR path already has one at comment_wake.ex:56-57), move test seams out of the event map into an opts keyword, and assert on the recorded write instead of log text. Keep log assertions only for unique sentinel strings.
findings.refactor_hint: Seams inside domain event maps leak test concerns into the event contract that webhooks and polling share; separating them makes the event shape a clean package boundary.

findings.title: Tests read the real checkout and real environment: Config.repo() git-origin fallback; GITHUB_TOKEN deleted and not restored
findings.description: planning_source_test (no TestSupport, so no configured repo) calls `Config.repo()` 8 times; `repo/0` falls back to `Aiur.Git.origin_repo()`, i.e. the git remote of the directory `mix test` runs in. On a checkout without an origin (a tarball, a fresh `git init`, some CI caches) it returns nil and `String.replace(@pack, "acme/widgets", nil)` raises, so the tests pass or fail on the host rather than the code. init/github_test deletes GITHUB_TOKEN (and on_exit deletes it again) in 6 tests without saving the previous value, so an operator or CI token present at suite start is gone for every later test in the VM.
findings.evidence: planning_source_test.exs:142 `repository = Config.repo()` then :145 `String.replace(@pack, "acme/widgets", String.upcase(repository))`. config.ex:30 `def repo(opts) when is_list(opts), do: explicit_repo() || origin_repo(opts)`; :173-174 `defp resolve_origin_repo do case Aiur.Git.origin_repo() do`. github_test.exs:324-325 `System.delete_env("GITHUB_TOKEN"); on_exit(fn -> System.delete_env("GITHUB_TOKEN") end)`; other files in the unit restore correctly (comment_polling_test.exs:8-17).
findings.recommendation: Pin the repository in planning_source_test (configure `tracker.github.repo` or use `Config.repo(origin_fun: fn -> "owner/repo" end)`). In github_test save and restore GITHUB_TOKEN with the shared `put_system_env!` helper (tests-3-09).
findings.refactor_hint: Build-order web code depending on the GitHub config's git-origin fallback is a cross-package reach (aiur_web -> GitHub config -> Git); pass the repository into PlanningSource explicitly.

findings.title: VM-global cwd, PATH and XDG/OPENCODE env mutated while application processes run
findings.description: `File.cd!/2` changes the working directory of the whole BEAM; it is used 9 times in 4 init test files because the production functions read the cwd implicitly (Dotenv.load/0, Scaffold.ensure_env/1, GitHub.detect_repo/0, Runtime.detect_toolchain/0, Runtime.setup_repo_state/1). server_test prepends a stub `opencode` directory to PATH and sets OPENCODE_CONFIG/OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT/XDG_* for the VM. The modules are sync, but supervised application processes (WorkflowStore reloads, Git origin resolution, any slot/prewarm spawn) keep running and resolve relative paths or spawn `opencode` during those windows. server_test's prepare_serve_root/0 also builds its tmp dir without System.pid, contrary to TestSupport.tmp_root!/1's documented cross-VM collision.
findings.evidence: dotenv_test.exs:38 `File.cd!(dir, fn -> Dotenv.load() end)`; scaffold_test.exs:41,48,65,76; github_test.exs:388,399; runtime_test.exs:27,57. server_test.exs:328 `System.put_env("PATH", stub_dir <> ":" <> original_path)`; :46 `System.put_env(child_env)`; :356-360 `Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "aiur-opencode-reap-#{System.unique_integer(...)}")`.
findings.recommendation: Give the init functions a `cwd:`/`root:` option and pass the tmp dir; give Opencode.Server an `env:`/`executable:` option so tests pass the stub path and XDG dirs to the Port instead of mutating the VM env. Use tmp_root!/1 for all tmp dirs.
findings.refactor_hint: Explicit cwd/env parameters are a prerequisite for moving `aiur init` and the opencode launcher into separate packages or CLIs.

findings.title: Untagged tests need real binaries and OS processes (opencode, bash, pgrep, ps, git) with 15-40 s waits
findings.description: server_test boots a real `opencode serve` (Server.start_link -> `exec opencode serve --port 0`), talks HTTP to it and reads its sqlite db; it waits up to 40 s for startup. retry_engine_test spawns `bash -c 'sleep 600 & wait'` and polls `pgrep -P` to find the child. github_test runs `git init`/`git remote add` and ignores the exit status. orphaned_workers_test runs real AgentRunner tasks on the app TaskSupervisor with 15 s waits. None are tagged, while test_helper only excludes `:external`, `:perf_regression`, `:quarantine` and `:real_proc` (on hosts without /proc), so on a host without opencode on PATH these fail rather than skip, and they dominate suite wall time.
findings.evidence: server_test.exs:254 `assert_receive {:serve_up, server, os_pid}, 40_000`; :403-409 boot_serve. retry_engine_test.exs:1027 `Port.open({:spawn_executable, String.to_charlist(bash)}, [:binary, args: [~c"-c", ~c"sleep 600 & wait"]])`; :1091 `System.cmd(pgrep, ["-P", ...])`. github_test.exs:385-386 `System.cmd("git", ["init"], cd: dir)` result discarded. test_helper.exs:55 `ExUnit.start(exclude: [:external, :perf_regression, :quarantine] ++ real_proc_exclude)`. Receive-timeout histogram in the unit: 5000 ms ×8, 15000 ms ×2, 40000 ms ×1.
findings.recommendation: Tag these `@tag :real_proc` (or a new `:needs_opencode`) and skip with a clear reason when the binary is absent; assert on System.cmd exit codes. Keep one integration test per behaviour and cover the rest with the stub executable approach already used at server_test.exs:298-352.
findings.refactor_hint: Integration tests that need the opencode binary should live with the opencode package's integration suite, not in the unit suite every package runs.

findings.title: `@tag :not_async` is used 7 times but nothing reads it; ExUnit async is module-level
findings.description: The tag suggests per-test serialisation, but ExUnit decides concurrency per module (`use ExUnit.Case, async: ...`) and no test_helper/CI config filters on `:not_async`. Both modules happen to be sync because `use ExUnit.Case` defaults to async: false, so the tag is dead and would give false confidence if someone flips the module to async.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn not_async` finds only the 7 `@tag :not_async` lines; test_helper.exs:55 excludes [:external, :perf_regression, :quarantine, :real_proc].
findings.recommendation: Delete the tags and write `use ExUnit.Case, async: false` explicitly with a one-line reason (env mutation).
findings.refactor_hint: None beyond cleanup.

findings.title: GitHub HTTP double setup copied between the two blocked_by regression files and reaching into a private persistent_term key
findings.description: Both files repeat the same ~45-line setup: ensure :req started, save 3-4 app keys, start a private Quota, point `:github_transport_test_options` at Req.Test, disable the budget, erase the cached token, put GITHUB_TOKEN, write a github workflow, reset ResourceStore, and restore everything. Tree-wide 9 test files set `:github_transport_test_options` and 56 put GITHUB_TOKEN. Both erase `{Aiur.GitHub.Config, :resolved_token}` directly (21 test files tree-wide do this) because GitHub.Config has no reset API; they leave the sibling key `:resolved_token_source` in place, which `token_source/0` still reads.
findings.evidence: dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test.exs:17 `@token_cache_key {Aiur.GitHub.Config, :resolved_token}` ... :37 `:persistent_term.erase(@token_cache_key)`; dispatcher_stale_blocked_by_test.exs:25,43 identical. config.ex:273-274 writes both `:resolved_token` and `:resolved_token_source`; :295 `(source = :persistent_term.get({__MODULE__, :resolved_token_source}, nil)) in [:env, :keyring]`.
findings.recommendation: Extract `Aiur.Test.GitHubDouble.setup!(repo: ..., label_prefix: ...)` returning the stub name, and add `Aiur.GitHub.Config.reset_token_cache/0` (clears both keys) for tests; replace the 21 direct persistent_term pokes.
findings.refactor_hint: The GitHub client package should ship its own test double and cache-reset API; consumers (orchestrator, build order, web) then depend on that instead of the private cache key.

findings.title: ≈11 s of guaranteed idle wait per run from negative receives, mostly after synchronous calls
findings.description: 61 `refute_receive` without a timeout (100 ms each) plus 51 with explicit timeouts summing 5,080 ms: about 11.2 s of pure waiting in this unit, most of it in sync modules that run serially. In files like merged_ticket_reconciler_test (15 bare refutes) and comment_wake_test (15) the callbacks are invoked synchronously in the test process, so `refute_received` is equivalent and instant; where the sender is asynchronous, a 100 ms refute cannot prove absence anyway.
findings.evidence: Parser over the unit: refute_receive total 112, bare 61; timed refutes 51 totalling 5,080 ms. merged_ticket_reconciler_test.exs:95-120 reconcile/3 is called synchronously with `update_issue_state_fun` sending to `parent` before `refute_receive {:transition, "1570"}`.
findings.recommendation: Use `refute_received` (optionally after the issue_sync_test `mailbox_barrier/0` pattern) for synchronous producers; for asynchronous ones, synchronise on a positive completion signal first and then `refute_received`.
findings.refactor_hint: None; local speed-up that also makes intent clearer.

findings.title: `@tag config: @enabled` repeated 45 times instead of @moduletag; lifetime_dispatch_budget_test re-implements TestSupport isolation by hand
findings.description: lifetime_dispatch_budget_test writes `@tag config: @enabled` before 30 tests (two override it at 670 and 720) and auto_resume_test does so 15 times. lifetime_dispatch_budget_test's 45-line setup saves and restores `:workflow_file_path`, `:dispatch_budget_store_path`, `:decision_state_dir`, `:log_file` with four copies of the same if/else, i.e. a second, divergent implementation of the TestSupport per-test workflow root.
findings.evidence: `grep -c '@tag config: @enabled'` = 30 (lifetime) and 15 (auto_resume). lifetime_dispatch_budget_test.exs:28-54 four `if is_nil(previous_x) do Application.delete_env ... else Application.put_env ...` blocks.
findings.recommendation: Use `@moduletag config: @enabled` with per-test overrides, and the shared put_app_env!/workflow helper (tests-3-09).
findings.refactor_hint: None.

findings.title: Struct-shape and type-only assertions where a value is the point
findings.description: `assert %State{} = result` (reconciler_test 439 is the last assertion of 'resolves a divergence before removing a terminal ticket' and does not check the ticket was removed), `assert is_integer(next.decision_store_unavailable_since_ms)`, `assert is_pid(state.ci_readiness_check_pid)`, `assert is_integer(state.ci_readiness_retry_at_ms)` (the retry delay value is what the test is about), `assert %DateTime{} = ...measured_at`, `is_map/is_function/has_key?` for runtime_deps, `is_binary(admission.semantic_key)`. Counts in the unit: is_integer 16, is_reference 10, is_binary 8, is_pid 6, is_map 3, struct-only matches 6. Several sit next to value assertions and are fine; the listed ones are the only check of the behaviour they name.
findings.evidence: reconciler_test.exs:439 `assert %State{} = result` (test at 394-440 never checks `result.running`); dispatcher_test.exs:882 `assert is_integer(state.ci_readiness_retry_at_ms)`.
findings.recommendation: Assert the value the behaviour produces (e.g. `refute Map.has_key?(result.running, issue.id)`, the retry deadline relative to an injected now) and mutation-check per AGENTS.md.
findings.refactor_hint: None.

findings.title: Assertions run inside a spawned production process in tts_test
findings.description: The injected `request` function runs inside the process `TTS.start/3` spawns, and it contains `assert {:cont, {_request, _response}} = into.(...)`. A failed assertion there raises in the TTS process, not the test, so the test fails later on a missing message (100 ms bare assert_receive) with an unrelated error, or passes if the crash path still sends the expected messages.
findings.evidence: tts_test.exs:16-17 `assert {:cont, {_request, _response}} = into.({:data, <<1, 2>>}, {request, response})` inside `request = fn url, options -> ... end`, which TTS invokes from its own process (the test monitors that pid at :28).
findings.recommendation: Send the `into` results to the test process and assert there, and wait with an explicit timeout or monitor.
findings.refactor_hint: None.

findings.title: webhook_mode_contract_test locates consumer tests by a relative path walk tied to the current tree layout
findings.description: The meta-test enforces that every `consumer_*_test.exs` uses the dual-mode harness by globbing `Path.expand("../../../test/aiur/webhooks", __DIR__)`. Moving the webhooks tests into a package changes the directory; the 'at least one consumer test file' test would then fail loudly (good), but the path climbs out of test/ and back in, so it silently couples to `src/` being the mix project root.
findings.evidence: webhook_mode_contract_test.exs:19 `@consumer_dir Path.expand("../../../test/aiur/webhooks", __DIR__)`; :122 `defp consumer_files, do: @consumer_dir |> Path.join(@consumer_glob) |> Path.wildcard()`.
findings.recommendation: Use `Path.join(__DIR__, "consumer_*_test.exs")` so the check travels with the directory.
findings.refactor_hint: Update when the webhooks package is carved.
